facts.statement: The type species of Undorosaurus grew to be 4 to 6 meters long.
facts.quote: It was a large ichthyosaur, with the type species measuring 4 - 6 m long.

facts.statement: Vladimir M. Efimov named the genus Undorosaurus in 1999, with Undorosaurus gorodischensis as the type species.
facts.quote: Undorosaurus was named by Vladimir M. Efimov in 1999 and the type species is Undorosaurus gorodischensis.

facts.statement: The genus was first known from holotype UPM EP-II-20 (527), a partial skeleton with a partial skull preserved in three dimensions.
facts.quote: Undorosaurus was first known from the holotype UPM EP-II-20 (527), a partial three-dimensionally preserved skeleton which preserved partial skull.

facts.statement: The holotype was collected near the Volga River at Gorodischi from the Epivirgatites nikitini ammonoid zone of the Late Jurassic.
facts.quote: It was collected near the Volga river at Gorodischi from the Epivirgatites nikitini ammonoid zone, dating to the Late Jurassic.

facts.statement: The species U. trautscholdi was discovered in 1878 by Hermann Trautschold and formally described in 2014 based on a partial left forefin from Mnyovniki, Moscow Oblast.
facts.quote: A second species, U. trautscholdi, was discovered in 1878 by Hermann Trautschold and was described by M.S. Arkhangelsky and N.G. Zverkov in 2014 from a partial left forefin found in the locality of Mnyovniki (village), Moscow Oblast.

facts.statement: The third species, U. kielanae, was first described by Daniel Tyborowski in 2016 as Cryopterygius kielanae from the Kcynia Formation in Poland.
facts.quote: The holotype (specimen GMUL UŁ no. 3579-81) of the third species, U. kielanae, was discovered in the Kcynia Formation of the Owadów-Brzezinki Quarry, Poland, and it was first described by Daniel Tyborowski in 2016 as Cryopterygius kielanae.

facts.statement: Chris McGowan and Ryosuke Motani (2003) identified an incompletely fused ischiopubis and remarkably strong dentition as key differences from Ophthalmosaurus, supporting Undorosaurus as a valid genus.
facts.quote: Chris McGowan and Ryosuke Motani (2003) pointed out two noteworthy differences to Ophthalmosaurus, an incompletely fused ischiopubis and a remarkably strong dentition, and considered Undorosaurus to be a valid genus of ophthalmosaurid.

facts.statement: Zverkov and Efimov (2019) treated the genus Cryopterygius as a junior synonym of Undorosaurus.
facts.quote: Zverkov & Efimov (2019) considered the genus Cryopterygius to be a junior synonym of the genus Undorosaurus.

facts.statement: Undorosaurus belongs to the family Ophthalmosauridae.
Undorosaurus lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Oxfordian to Tithonian (161.5 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Cryopterygius kristiansenae is synonymous with Undorosaurus gorodischensis.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that C. kristiansenae may also be synonymous with Undorosaurus.

rejected.statement: Undorosaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur found in western Russia, Svalbard, and Poland.
rejected.quote: Undorosaurus is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur known from western Russia, Svalbard, and Poland.
